title: Building Tiny Forge with my 10-year-old son and Codex — Season 1 is playable
author: Patwater0
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/id8gfhip8iuh1.jpg?width=1265&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=1ab23ef76031ad929cf82516313aa622ca0163d7

Hey everyone! My 10-year-old son is interested in game development and AI, and Tiny Forge started as a project for us to explore that together. It’s now a playable browser dungeon runner, and Season 1 started October 8.

Most of the code was developed with Codex, and we used AI image tools for the game artwork. The art work included enemy sprite sheets, dungeon backgrounds, bosses, and modular hero/equipment pieces. The game is hosted on Cloudflare. AI also helped me put this post together.

The interesting part of this update has been deciding what to simplify after people actually played it. A player described sorting through hundreds of drops to find useful socket bases. We added a loot filter with rarity, socket, and stat/skill requirements, plus optional auto-salvage for new drops. That felt like a more useful thing to work on than adding another system.

We also added a gear comparison that can show both items at upgrade level zero, so a new drop gets a fair comparison with something you’ve already upgraded. We removed the auction house, chat lobby, and crafting UI because they weren’t getting much use and were crowding the interface. Alongside that, we’ve been fixing interrupted spoils screens and cloud-save issues.

The loop is automatic combat, choosing gear and skills, and deciding how far to push each expedition. It’s very much inspired by the Diablo “one more run” feeling. Season 1 has a fresh leaderboard, and you can try it as a guest without registering: [https://tinyforge.gg](https://tinyforge.gg)

I’d love some playtesting feedback, especially on whether the first few runs make sense and whether the loot decisions are interesting. For anyone else building with AI: how are you deciding when to cut a feature versus spending more time improving it?
